problems.title: Rotating a closed tour creates an impossible positive label
problems.source_location: Task 2, arXiv v1 PDF p. 4; Appendix B.1.2, pp. 15–16; data_gen.py compare_routes, lines 185–218.
claim: Task \(2\), PDF p. 4 and Appendix B.1.2, PDF pp. 15–16, defines a positive candidate as an optimal next-node connection. Released sample_codes/1_data_gen/data_gen.py, compare_routes, rotates closed tours to align them while retaining their repeated terminal vertex.
analysis: Take the simple closed tour lists \(O=(0,6,1,2,3,4,5,0)\) and \(G=(0,6,3,1,2,4,5,0)\), aligned from vertex \(4\). The source forward rotation makes \(O\) into \((4,5,0,0,6,1,2,3)\), while the greedy sequence begins \((4,5,0,6,\ldots)\). Their first reported divergence is therefore \[(\mathrm{current},\mathrm{negative},\mathrm{positive})=(0,6,0)\]. A self-edge cannot be a next unvisited choice in any Hamiltonian cycle; moreover \(\{0,6\}\) is an edge of the supplied optimal tour.

Rotating only the distinct cycle vertices instead yields the first divergence \((6,3,1)\). The defect is preservation of cycle representation, before any probe fit. The paper describes an additional constrained-optimality filter that is absent from this sample path and could protect a different historical pipeline.
result: The current sample generator can create an impossible supervised target, but its exposure in the original filtered probing datasets is unresolved.
repair: Remove the repeated closure endpoint before modular rotation or reversal; validate distinct candidates and source-tour adjacency, then perform the stated forced-negative and forbidden-positive optimization checks.
problems.impact_rationale: The current sample generator can create an impossible supervised target, but its exposure in the original filtered probing datasets is unresolved.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Held-out rows are not held-out routing instances
problems.source_location: Appendix B.2.1, arXiv v1 PDF p. 17; example_probing_exp.ipynb cells 7 and 15.
claim: Appendix B.2.1, PDF p. 17, describes training/test splits but does not require grouping by routing instance. The released probing notebook creates a positive and a negative Task \(2\) row for each instance, then splits rows rather than instance identifiers.
analysis: Positive and negative probe rows share one underlying routing instance and embeddings. Splitting rows independently can put one member into training and the paired member into testing. The resulting score measures held-out rows, not generalization to independent routing instances; grouping by instance is required for that interpretation.
result: The released split supports generalization to held-out rows, not necessarily new routing instances. The paper does not explicitly state the stronger grouping rule, and the historical score inflation is not quantified.
repair: If the intended claim concerns unseen routing instances, assign and retain an instance_id before creating rows. Split those IDs, or use GroupShuffleSplit, and place every row and every repeated extraction from an instance in the same partition. For model comparisons, preserve the same grouped split across models and layers. Any hyperparameter selection or feature selection must remain within training groups.
problems.impact_rationale: The row split permits shared source instances; a stricter unseen-instance estimand and any numerical AUC change are not established.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The released plotting cell does not identify the stated adjusted-significance analysis
problems.source_location: Adjusted-significance statement, PDF p. 8; released sample notebook, cell 19.
claim: The paper's PDF p. 8 states Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control over \(256\) dimensions; the released sample notebook's cell 19 marks raw p-values.
analysis: Raw thresholds do not implement BH adjustment. However, an unadjusted example cell does not prove the correction was never run elsewhere. The complete p-value family, correction operation and adjusted output are needed to verify the reported adjusted decisions.
result: Evidence gap concerning historical adjusted-significance provenance; no substitute significance verdict is supplied.
assumptions: Bounded to the stated source/component; no published-run provenance inferred.
problems.impact_rationale: The visible raw-p-value plotting path cannot verify the claimed adjusted decisions, but it does not prove that adjustment was absent elsewhere.

impact_rationale: The latest paper/current sample code retain a label-generation defect and a row-versus-instance holdout limitation. Original dataset exposure and adjusted-significance provenance remain unresolved; central representation results are not recomputed.
